text:
deploy-bot: ALERT — canary error-rate spike detected for prompt-router -> new-endpoint (prompt-v3).
deploy-bot: metric: canary: prompt-v3-prod (10% traffic) 
```
error_rate: 12.7% (baseline 0.8%)
5xx_count: 342
latency_p95: 1.9s (was 0.4s)
logs: /var/log/prompt-router/new-endpoint/2026-03-15.log
```
oncall-bot: Paging zach (SRE on-call) — urgent. :rotating_light: @zach please ack.
zach: Acked, looking. pulling up metrics and logs now.
maria: tagging infra/sre — this looks like the canary we cut 08:14UTC to route 10% to the experimental prompt-v3 endpoint. Seeing traffic errors right after.
sriram: quick hypothesis: new endpoint returning a bad model artifact under specific context lengths -> 5xx from runtime. If true, flip routing FF rather than full rollback.
alyssa-pm: customer-facing? Any active customer incidents? Support channel not yet. I can check telemetry.
zach: tailing logs, seeing a repeated stacktrace: 
```
RuntimeError: KV cache overflow at step 0x1f3
  at serve.py:482
  at handler.py:210
```
zach: Also seeing resource OOMs on a subset of the new-pool nodes. Likely kernel mismatch with quantized build.
maria: we should hit the emergency feature-flag kill-switch for prompt routing to divert traffic back to stable immediately. This avoids a full code rollback and is faster.
sriram: agreed. Command to flip: 
```
# from admin jumpbox
redwood-ff toggle --env prod --flag feature.prompt_route_new_endpoint --off --reason "canary 5xx spike"
```
zach: I'm going to run the toggle now, will monitor.
devops-bot: Executing requested FF toggle...
devops-bot: Command: redwood-ff toggle --env prod --flag feature.prompt_route_new_endpoint --off --actor zach
devops-bot: SUCCESS — flag feature.prompt_route_new_endpoint set to OFF in prod (propagation ~5s).
zach: seeing traffic shift in the router: new-endpoint traffic down to 0. Stable route back to prompt-v2. Error rate dropping.

deploy-bot: Canary error_rate now 0.9% (close to baseline). 5xx_count trending down. Latency p95 back to 0.45s.
alyssa-pm: Do we have customer impact? Support reports 3 customers with transient errors, all on the canary cohort. Escalated to SRE but now stabilized. I'll draft a brief customer note.
maria: Good. We'll keep the FF off until a patch is validated. Who will own the follow-up?
jordan: I'll take lead on postmortem / root cause & validate artifact build matrix. Will coordinate with ML infra and model team.
sriram: plan: reproduce locally with the same quantization kernel combo, run unit tests for kv cache boundary, and produce a fixed artifact.
alyssa-pm: I'll prepare incident summary and outreach. Suggest severity SEV3 (limited customers, mitigated by FF toggle).
zach: handoff to jordan for remediation. I'm staying on to help reproduce. If anything regresses I'll reopen.
maria: thanks all. Adding checklist items:
- [x] Kill-switch activated (zach)
- [x] Traffic routed back to stable (router)
- [x] Customers identified and notified (alyssa)
- [ ] Patch & QA (jordan + sriram)
- [ ] Postmortem in #postmortems (due 48h)

devops-bot: Note: audit entry created for FF toggle by zach at 2026-03-15T08:17:04Z. ref: audit/ff/2198765432
jordan: I'll set up a repro job and invite model infra; will post updates in this thread.
zach: re-ack oncall — I'm handing off active monitoring to jordan. If pager triggers before I sign back in, page me back. :thumbsup:
maria: closing the live incident channel. Moving to follow-up. Thanks team. :heart:
